correctness.rationale: For each vertex, the isolation indicator is its own Bernoulli mark times absence of every neighbor. This proves the exact first/joint moments and sign law. A distance-two pair gives q from a positive moment ratio. Without any distance-two pair the graph is a union of cliques, and distinct component orders give q from means; identical nontrivial clique sizes give exactly the unimodal two-root ambiguity of p(1-p)^(k-1), including at the full-law level. A union bound proves finite-sample recovery. Every graph through five vertices was enumerated at two exact rational probabilities, yielding 102616 checks, supplementing rather than replacing the proof.

value.rationale: Determining exact identifiability when only retained isolated-node indicators are recorded is a natural inverse site-percolation problem. For every graph the second-order sign geometry reveals all adjacencies and distance-two relations even with unknown p, and the full-law obstruction is completely classified as one homogeneous family with a sharp parameter exception. This is not just an isolated finite value; the decoder and valid global finite-sample guarantee make the classification operational, subject to explicitly stated assumptions.
